### 1. 2026-11-17 12:44 UTC

> Explore `/run-brief` and describe all options that can be passed when invoking a run to me

**Reply:**

`/run-brief` takes four arguments. Its signature, from `.claude/skills/run-brief/SKILL.md`:

```
/run-brief [--no-foundation] [--unattended] [--summary-interval SECONDS] <NAME | llm-dlc/loops/NAME.md>
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`<brief>`** (required) | The one brief to run, given by name (`domain-advances`) or by file (`llm-dlc/loops/domain-advances.md`). If the request doesn't clearly name one brief, the watcher asks before starting anything. A brief whose status is already `done` isn't run. |
| **`--no-foundation`** | Skips stage 2, the Fable 5.2 session that builds the shared groundwork and updates the plan before the streams start. Stage 2 is also skipped without this flag if a foundation has already landed or a stream's workspace already exists, because that means an earlier run is being continued. |
| **`--unattended`** | Tells the watcher you're away for the whole run. It doesn't bring you anything it can decide and record itself. A question only you can answer is recorded as an open decision (`decisions.py record`, state `open`), and the rest of the run carries on around it. This also covers test failures after a merge, or a foundation that changed what the brief is for: these become open decisions instead of stopping the run. |

### 2. 2026-11-17 13:13 UTC

> There seems to be issues with `RUN_STREAMS_WATCHER` in my latest feature brief, that is distracting agents from their goal. Check tmux win0 for watcher and da-* windows for other agents. Is this something we can fix without affecting the work in progress? We can look into a more strategic fix after it's done.

**Reply:**

Yes, it's fixed, and nothing that is running was changed. From each stream's next turn on, its sessions see `RUN_STREAMS_WATCHER` as empty, so the leaking test can no longer reach your watcher.

**What I found:** The watcher (win 0) had already worked this out and fixed the test on the main line (`smxzwqlr`). The four streams branched before that fix, so their copy of `test_brief_run.py` still passes the variable on. Whenever a stream ran its tests, the test's made-up run posted fake "merge stream a/b?" questions to the real watcher, then hung or failed. So far 11 or more questions have come in, all answered `leave`. The da-* windows show the cost: preservation, challenge and state each stopped to diagnose the failure and rerun the test with the variable unset.

**The fix:** I added `.claude/settings.local.json` to each stream workspace (state, evidence, preservation, challenge). It sets `RUN_STREAMS_WATCHER` to empty for that workspace's Claude sessions.
- **Nothing running is touched.** `run-streams.sh` keeps its own copy of the variable, so merge and blocked questions from the real streams still reach the watcher. Only the sessions it starts lose it, and nothing they run needs it.
- **Takes effect at each stream's next turn.** The loop starts a fresh `claude -p` for every turn, and that process reads the file. Turns already in progress keep the old value until they end.

### 4. 2026-11-17 14:29 UTC

> Write a summary on preservation chasing a failing gap scan test (read-only) for me to reference in a blog post: An hour and a half in, at $54.22. Preservation hasn't committed for 30 minutes because it is chasing a failing gap-scan test before its next commit. The other three streams are committing steadily. Still watching. -- put the summary in `../docs`, the purpose will be to compare model sizes and show why complexity of task matters relative to model

**Reply:**

I've written the summary to `~/code/docs/preservation-gap-scan-2026-11-17.md`. The `docs` folder didn't exist, so I created it. I only read the session record and the run log; I didn't touch the preservation stream.

**The watcher's framing doesn't hold up.** Preservation went 43 minutes without a commit, from 13:47 to 14:30. Only about 7 of those minutes went on the failing gap-scan test, starting at 14:23. Before that it made real progress:
- It modelled warning-level logging in the checker, with countermodels it ran on a real JVM.
- It deliberately weakened its own soundness check to confirm the tests would catch it.
- It modelled `String.valueOf(Object)` for a string or null argument.
- It probed example 287 at the claim's real bound and reached both versions' bcrypt. The probe failed there in the way the brief predicted.

**What made the test failure a subtle mistake:**
- The checker asks "can I run this call?" in two places: a scan that only sees the bytecode, and the engine, which sees the argument values. Both read one shared list of modelled calls.
- The agent added `String.valueOf(Object)` to that list. That made the scan claim the call is handled for every argument, when the engine only handles a string or null.
- It was following the entry next to it: `Pattern.compile` is already on the list, though it is also only modelled for some arguments.
- An existing test about 2,000 lines away holds the stricter rule. That test, not the model, caught the unsound change.

About an hour and a half into the run, it is on track. The streams are working the way the brief asked: they reproduce a problem before fixing it, check each countermodel on a real JVM, and get answers counted only through `accept.py`. They are also finding real problems.

The research goals at the centre of the brief (M2 and the end of M3) have only just been reached, though. Expect those to end as recorded walls rather than decided claims. The brief counts that as a valid outcome.
